assumptions: api-gateway upstream connection pool keepalive idle timeout is equal to or greater than backend HTTP server idle connection timeouts.
api-gateway route proxy configuration does not enable retries on upstream connection reset for idempotent requests.
top.mechanism: api-gateway maintains pooled persistent HTTP connections to upstream microservices (portfolio-service, orders-service, and quotes-service). When an upstream backend closes an idle socket due to its local keepalive idle timeout expiring at the exact moment api-gateway reuses the connection to forward a request, the backend kernel responds with a TCP RST. Because api-gateway lacks an automatic retry policy on upstream connection reset, the reset immediately returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway to web-app. The 14 reset events logged by api-gateway across portfolio-service (11) and orders-service (3) between 18:56 and 19:47 UTC directly align with the 14 support tickets between 19:00 and 19:30 UTC, while retries on fresh sockets succeeded. Earlier resets against quotes-service confirm a generalized gateway upstream connection pool management race condition rather than backend degradation.
top.title: Keep-alive idle connection timeout mismatch and missing retry policy on api-gateway

assumptions: api-gateway maintains an upstream HTTP keep-alive connection pool whose idle timeout is equal to or longer than the server-side idle timeout on backend services (portfolio-service, orders-service, quotes-service).
api-gateway does not automatically retry requests when receiving a TCP reset before response headers (lacks retry_on: reset).
Static container or reverse-proxy keepalive configurations cannot be queried via runtime_config due to tooling scope.
top.mechanism: api-gateway maintains persistent HTTP keepalive connections to upstream services (portfolio-service, orders-service, and quotes-service). When api-gateway's upstream connection idle timeout is equal to or exceeds the backend servers' keepalive timeout, a race condition occurs: an upstream backend closes an idle TCP connection (sending TCP FIN) at the exact moment api-gateway reuses the connection to dispatch a new client request from web-app. The backend kernel drops incoming data on the half-closed socket and responds with TCP RST. api-gateway logs 'upstream reset before headers', fails to retry the request, and returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway to web-app. Web-app surfaces the 502 to users on /portfolio and /orders. Retries succeed immediately because a fresh TCP handshake is established. Telemetry confirms resets occur sporadically across multiple services throughout the day (at 16:56, 16:57, 17:37, 17:58, 18:16, 18:56, 19:05, 19:18, 19:24, 19:31, and 19:47 UTC), while all backend services remain completely healthy.

The upstream responds with TCP RST, causing api-gateway to record 'upstream reset before headers' and emit an HTTP 502 Bad Gateway to web-app due to the absence of retry policies on connection resets.

The new real-time P&L logic executes an unbatched per-symbol query ('SELECT * FROM fills WHERE account_id = <N> AND symbol = $<N>') against orders-db, driving portfolio-service's db_queries_per_request up by over 13x from ~3 to ~41 (met-541ecab0, met-ad7bd70e). At steady incoming request traffic of ~140 rps (met-646bd103), this introduced >5,700 additional queries/sec into orders-db, pushing orders-db queries_per_sec from ~1,185 to ~8,903-9,920 qps (met-834ce1f7, met-e0e1ef5a). orders-db CPU saturated at 97-100% (met-0ecaf57b, met-f0276915) and active connections jumped to ~176-198 (met-66206bf4, met-ed60061a) with 960 logged slow queries attributed to app=portfolio-service (logpat-54f247b0, log-c31d932356). As a result of database resource and connection saturation, orders-service suffered connection acquisition timeouts (logpat-b346b9ea, log-f1a298ed44), causing orders-service p99 latency to surge to ~3.5s (met-204bb042, met-0ded8d15) and error rate to rise to ~6% (met-a4617af2, met-73b8d8f5).

assumptions: api-gateway keep-alive idle connection timeout exceeds backend timeouts, or api-gateway lacks proxy_next_upstream retry handling on connection reset before headers.

top.mechanism: api-gateway maintains persistent HTTP keep-alive connections to backend services (portfolio-service, orders-service). When a backend server closes an idle connection after its keepalive timeout expires, and api-gateway dispatches a new request on that connection before receiving the FIN packet, the backend kernel responds with a TCP RST. api-gateway logs 'upstream reset before headers' and returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway to web-app instead of retrying on a fresh connection. Subsequent retries succeed immediately because a fresh TCP connection is negotiated. This mechanism explains the sporadic low failure rate (~0.5%), baseline occurrences prior to 19:00 UTC, and normal health metrics across all backend services.

Under steady baseline ingestion (~2.5 MB/s, met-ef2be348), log segments that would have expired after 72 hours accumulated on disk. At exactly 06:45:00 UTC (72 hours after cfg-0003), broker disk reached 100% capacity (met-08403145), causing 'No space left on device' write errors (log-c45ec54c2c). This caused 18 partitions across orders.fills and ledger.postings to become under-replicated (met-378e9ed4, logpat-14977dc0, logpat-32262242) and produce error rates to spike to >34% (met-ccc4bee3), triggering NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS errors in upstream producers orders-service (log-107b867338) and payments-service (log-1ab631d747). Downstream consumers notification-service and ledger-service could not consume new events from stalled partitions, causing consumer lag to surge (>62k and >73k messages respectively) and confirmation emails / ledger postings to delay.
